classification.difficultyReason: Find roots from the factors, connect their midpoint to the symmetry axis, substitute to obtain the vertex and y-intercept, then interpret the leading coefficient to classify the extremum and sketch. The listed tasks scaffold this routine chain.

inlines.text: For each of the following quadratics
find the coordinates of the vertex.
state whether the vertex is a maximum or a minimum.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x-2)(x-6)\\x&=2\text{ or }6\\y(0)&=(0-2)(0-6)\\y(0)&=12\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{2+6}{2}=4\\y(4)&=(4-2)(4-6)\\y(4)&=-4\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(4,-4)$. The parabola opens upwards, so its minimum $y$-value is $-4$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with roots 2 and 6, y-intercept 12 and dashed vertex guides at 4 and -4.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x+2)(x-6)\\x&=-2\text{ or }6\\y(0)&=(0+2)(0-6)\\y(0)&=-12\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-2+6}{2}=2\\y(2)&=(2+2)(2-6)\\y(2)&=-16\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(2,-16)$. The parabola opens upwards, so its minimum $y$-value is $-16$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with roots -2 and 6, symmetry guide x=2, y-intercept -12 and vertex height -16.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x+2)(x+6)\\x&=-2\text{ or }-6\\y(0)&=(0+2)(0+6)\\y(0)&=12\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-2-6}{2}=-4\\y(-4)&=(-4+2)(-4+6)\\y(-4)&=-4\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-4,-4)$. The parabola opens upwards, so its minimum $y$-value is $-4$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with roots -6 and -2, vertex guides at -4 and -4, and y-intercept 12.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-(x+2)(x-6)\\x&=-2\text{ or }6\\y(0)&=-(0+2)(0-6)\\y(0)&=12\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-2+6}{2}=2\\y(2)&=-(2+2)(2-6)\\y(2)&=16\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(2,16)$. The parabola opens downwards, so its maximum $y$-value is $16$.

spec.description: Downward parabola with roots -2 and 6, symmetry guide x=2, y-intercept 12 and maximum 16.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}0&=3(x+1)(x-7)\\x&=-1\text{ or }7\\y(0)&=3(0+1)(0-7)\\y(0)&=-21\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-1+7}{2}=3\\y(3)&=3(3+1)(3-7)\\y(3)&=-48\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(3,-48)$. The parabola opens upwards, so its minimum $y$-value is $-48$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with roots -1 and 7, symmetry guide x=3, y-intercept -21 and minimum -48.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-2(x-3)(x-5)\\x&=3\text{ or }5\\y(0)&=-2(0-3)(0-5)\\y(0)&=-30\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{3+5}{2}=4\\y(4)&=-2(4-3)(4-5)\\y(4)&=2\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(4,2)$. The parabola opens downwards, so its maximum $y$-value is $2$.

spec.description: Downward parabola with roots 3 and 5, vertex guides at 4 and 2, and y-intercept -30.
